Calculate the population size within length bins

Source: R/BLICC_Model.R
Rpop_len.Rd

The model integrates over growth rate variability and sums mortality piece-wise over intervening length intervals to derive the relative population number in each length bin taking into account variation in growth and varying mortality-at-length. This is analogous to an age based catch curve model, but for length. The model uses the Gauss-Laguerre quadrature rule for integration, so nodes and weights for this must be provided. This function is the same as Rpop_F, but does not return fishing mortality and is written in R.

Usage

Rpop_len(node, wt, Len, Zki, Galpha, Gbeta)

Arguments

node

Nodes for the Gauss-Laguerre quadrature rule

wt

Weights for the Gauss-Laguerre quadrature rule

Len

Vector of lower-bounds for length intervals

Zki

Vector of total mortality (in time units of growth rate parameter K) to be applied in each length interval. This vector should be the same length as Len

Galpha

Alpha parameter for the Gamma probability density function that governs growth variability.

Gbeta

Rate parameter for the Gamma distribution growth variability (=Galpha/Linf)

Value

A vector of population size in each length bin

Examples

glq <- statmod::gauss.quad(90, kind = "laguerre", alpha = 0.0)
S <- Rpop_len(glq$nodes, glq$weights, Len=15:55,
              Zki=c(rep(1.5, 10), rep(3, 31)), 100, 100/50)
plot(y=S, x=15:55, type="l")
